newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria gives rail comms contract to Israeli firm.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria gives rail comms contract to Israeli firm.

text.p: Nigeria's military government on Wednesday awarded a 2.64 billion naira ($325 million) contract to an Israeli firm to provide the African country's dilapidated railways with modern communication equipment.

"At the end of the rehabilitation exercise, Nigerians will no doubt witness an entirely new railway system," transport minister Major-General Ibrahim Gumel said at the signing of the contract with NAIRDA Telecommunications in the capital Abuja.

Gumel said the project, to be completed in 16 months, involved the supply and installation of Comprehensive Microwave Digital Backbone Communication that would allow for a train-to- train, station-to-train and station-to-station communication.
Staff training of Nigerians to use communication facilities was also part of the project, he added.
Work is already advanced in a separate $520 million rail rehabilitation contract awarded by the government in 1995 to state-run China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation.
The rail rehabilitation project by the Chinese involves total overhaul of tracks, delivery of locomotives and provision of technical expertise to Nigerian Railway Corporation.
Gumel said delivery of the locomotives would start in April.
Chinese officials said in January they would meet the target date of October 1998 to complete the project.
Nigerian railways have long been in ruins over lack of funding, with tracks unused and locomotives disabled. Government believes overhauling the sector would help revive the economy.

Nathan Gardner, spokesman for NAIRDA, said: "We are grateful to the Nigerian government for awarding us this contract. We will work in accordance with the terms and complete the project as scheduled."
